correctness.rationale: Uniform convergence of the falling-factorial interpolation and of all divided differences is controlled by factorial 2-adic divisibility. Odd inputs have derivative 1 mod 2, while even inputs have derivative 2 mod 4. Those congruences give exact valuation laws and three bijective isometric branches, whose finite quotient fiber sizes prove all multiplicities for every exponent. The least-period and 2-adic measure conclusions follow, with small levels separately enumerated. The embedded verifier tests every residue through exponent 15, but infinite validity follows from the proof.

Earlier derangement congruences, Hensel-type valuation methods, and interpolation do not state the explicit three-branch dyadic isometry and all-residue multiplicity classification. A previous exact-period result subsumes the period alone, so novelty attaches only to fiber multiplicities and range geometry. value.rationale: The exact all-level residue multiplicities give a complete and natural arithmetic classification for derangements. They distinguish the bijective even-residue branch from the fourfold odd-residue branch, determine exact support size at every 2-power and give a precise 2-adic Haar measure. Continuity and periodicity alone do not give these invariants, and the result has an explanatory structural isometry proof rather than a finite-data table.
